newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China-Taiwan shipping links to boost Taiwan economy.
newsitem.headline: China-Taiwan shipping links to boost Taiwan economy.

text.p: The resumption of direct shipping links between China and Taiwan will boost Taiwan's economic growth, a stock analyst said on Saturday.

"We see direct benefits for the Kaoshiung area of Taiwan which will handle most of shipping between there and ports on the eastern seaboard of the mainland (China)," Tina So, assistant director of Schroder Investment Management (Hong Kong) Ltd, told an investment seminar.

"Overall, the resumption of direct shipping and the closer economic tie that will stem from it could in time add as much as two percent a year to the growth rate of Taiwan's gross demestic product," she said.
Taiwan, which has banned direct links with China since 1949, has recently agreed to allow limited direct shipping with the mainland under its "offshore transshipment centre" scheme.
Beijing regards the Nationalist-held Taiwan as a renegade province and vows to bring it under China's eventual rule, by force if necessary.
Under the scheme, mainland cargoes are not allowed to enter Taiwan customs but can be transshipped at Kaohsiung for onward passage to third countries.
Likewise, Taiwan cargoes at Kaohsiung cannot be loaded on ships planning to cross directly to the Chinese mainland.
"Direct shipping links are also bound to generate a need for new infrastructure to handle the increased trade flow between the two economies (of China and Taiwan)," So said.
"We do not see Hong Kong suffering from the closer economic ties between China and Taiwan," she said.
Most trade between China and Taiwan passes through third countries, usually Hong Kong.
So said the increasing integration of the economies of China, Hong Kong and Taiwan is likely to lead to higher growth rates in the three places.

She noted the competitive advantages of Greater China -- low cost manufacturing in China, a developed port and international financial centre in Hong Kong, and the technical know-how and abundance of capital in Taiwan -- will together produce an increasing number of investment opportunties.
